You can plan trips that include stops for charging your electric vehicle (EV) and monitor changes in your charge while driving.

Important: EV routing is available on select vehicles and in select areas. Features vary by country and region. Refer to your vehicle’s owner guide for compatibility information.

When you get driving directions, Maps can track your vehicle’s charge. By analyzing elevation changes along the route and other factors, Maps identifies appropriate charging stations along the way, and, for select charging providers and countries, it provides real-time charging station availability. If you drive until your charge gets too low, you’re offered a route to the nearest compatible charging station.

Set up EV routing through CarPlay

For a compatible electric vehicle (EV) that doesn’t require an app from its manufacturer, use CarPlay to set up EV routing in the Maps app.

Note: Refer to the owner’s guide for your vehicle for compatibility information.

  1. Connect iPhone to CarPlay.
  2. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  3. Get driving directions.
  4. Tap Connect (above the list of routes), then follow the onscreen instructions.

See Intro to CarPlay and iPhone.

Set up EV routing using a vehicle manufacturer’s app

For a compatible vehicle that requires an app from its manufacturer, use the app to set up EV routing in Maps.

Note: Refer to the owner’s guide for your vehicle for compatibility information.

  1. Go to the App Store on your iPhone.

  2. Search for the manufacturer of your vehicle, then download the app that supports EV routing for it. (See Get apps in the App Store.)

  3. Open the app, then follow its setup instructions.

  4. Go to the Maps app , then tap your picture or initials next to the search field.

    If you don’t see your picture or initials, tap Cancel next to the search field, or tap the search field, then tap Cancel.

  5. Tap Vehicles, tap Connect Your Electric Vehicles, then follow the onscreen instructions.

You can designate a preferred charging network for your vehicle. The Maps app provides real-time charging station availability for select charging providers and countries, and you can search by plug type and network.

Choose a different vehicle when you get directions

If you drive several vehicles, you can change which vehicle Maps provides routing instructions for.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Get driving directions.
  3. Before you tap Go, scroll down in the route card.
  4. Choose another electric vehicle, or if you’re driving a vehicle that doesn’t have an EV routing app on your iPhone, tap Different Car.

See alsoGet driving directions in Maps on iPhoneChoose a default travel mode and Maps units on iPhone

Set your home, work, or school address

You can set your home, work, or school address for one-tap access to real-time traffic updates, directions, and notifications, making your travel more efficient.

Set your home, work, or school address

You can set a home or work address that’s different from the home or work address on your contact card in the Contacts app.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Below Places, tap [Image: the Add button] (you may need to swipe left).
  3. Tap the search field, then enter the address you’re looking for.
  4. Tap the address, then assign it to a type: My home, My work, or My school.
  5. Tap [Image: the Done button].

Note: If you change your home, work, or school address after you’re asked to sync Maps to My Card, you may need to update your address in Contacts. See Add or edit your home address.

Refine the location of an address

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Below Places, touch and hold the address you want to refine.
  3. Tap Edit Details.
  4. Tap Refine Location on the Map, then drag the map.
  5. Tap [Image: the Done button].

Change the details of a set address

You can change the details of your set addresses if those addresses change.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Below Places, touch and hold the address you want to change.

  3. Tap Edit Details, then do any of the following:

    • Change the name of the pin: Enter a new name in the Label field.
    • Assign the address to your home, work, or school: Choose an option below Type.
    • Change the location of the pin: Tap Refine Location on the Map.

Remove a set address

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Below Places, touch and hold the address you want to remove.
  3. Tap Unpin.

See alsoMark a location with a pin in Maps on iPhoneAdd or edit your contact info and photo on iPhone

Set your location and map view

You can find your location on a map and switch to different map views for different details. You can choose from Explore, Driving, Transit, and Satellite views. In select cities, Maps provides enhanced detail for elevation, roads, trees, buildings, landmarks, and more.

Note: Not all features are available in all countries or regions. For more information, see the iOS and iPadOS Feature Availability website.

WARNING: For important information about navigation and avoiding distractions that could lead to dangerous situations, see Important safety information.

Allow Maps to use your precise location

To find your location and provide accurate directions, iPhone must be connected to the internet, and Precise Location must be on.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Do one of the following:

    • If Maps displays a message that Location Services is off: Tap the message, tap Turn On in Settings, then turn on Location Services.
    • If Maps displays a message that Precise Location is off: Tap the message, tap Turn On in Settings, tap Location, then turn on Precise Location.

Cellular data rates may apply (see View or change cellular data settings).

Note: To get useful location-related information in Maps, leave Significant Locations turned on in Settings  > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services. See Find nearby attractions, restaurants, and services.

Show your current location

See Search for places to navigate from your current location to another.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the Tracking Off button].

    Your position is marked in the middle of the map. The top of the map is north.

    To show your heading instead of north at the top, tap [Image: the Tracking On button].

    To resume showing north, tap [Image: the Tracking On With Heading button] or [Image: the Compass button].

Switch to a different map view

The button at the lower right of a map indicates if the current map is for exploring , driving , riding transit , or in satellite view . You can change the map type at any time.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap the Map Modes button ([Image: the Exploring Map Mode button], [Image: the Driving Map Mode button], [Image: the Transit Map Mode button], [Image: the Satellite Map Mode button]) at the lower right.
  3. Choose another map type, then tap [Image: the Close button].

You can get driving, cycling, walking, and transit directions or get traffic and weather info in Maps.

Note: Apple is committed to keeping personal information about your location safe and private. Read more about Apple’s commitment: go to Settings  > Apps > Maps, then tap About Apple Maps & Privacy. You can also clear your location history or delete recent directions.

See alsoSet your home, work, or school address in Maps on iPhoneView a route overview or a list of turns in Maps on iPhoneShare your estimated time of arrival in Maps on iPhoneChoose a default travel mode and Maps units on iPhone

Share places

You can share places with others. For example, you can send a message or email to show people where to meet you.

Tip: To share your current location when you don’t have the Maps app open, just touch and hold the Maps icon on the Home Screen, then tap Send My Location. See Perform quick actions.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap a place on the map or a search result.
  3. Tap [Image: the Share button] (at the top of the place card), then choose an option.

You can also touch and hold the place, then tap Share Location.

See alsoSet your location and map view in Maps on iPhoneSearch for places in Maps on iPhoneCustomize sharing options in an iPhone app

Share your estimated time of arrival

You can share your estimated time of arrival (ETA) while following driving, cycling, and walking directions to let friends and family know when you’re likely to arrive. Your ETA updates automatically if there are major delays, so you don’t have to send follow-up messages along the way.

Note: Not all features are available in all countries or regions. See the iOS and iPadOS Feature Availability website.

Share your estimated time of arrival (ETA)

Siri: Ask Siri something like, “Share my ETA.” Learn how to use Siri.

Or without using Siri:

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Search for the place you want to go, then tap Go.

  3. Tap the route card at the bottom of the screen, then tap Share ETA.

    If you don’t see Share ETA, make sure you turned it on in Settings  > Apps > Maps.

  4. Choose one or more suggested contacts, or tap Open Contacts to find a contact.

  5. To share your ETA with more contacts, tap “Sharing with” at the bottom of the screen, then tap Open Contacts.

You can also use the Messages, Find My, and Contacts apps to share your ETA with others. See Share your location in Messages, Share your location in Find My, or Edit contacts.

Stop sharing your ETA

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Open the route card for a trip in progress.
  3. Tap “Sharing with” at the bottom of the screen, then tap Stop Sharing ETA below each contact’s name.

Automatically share your ETA to a pin

When you add a contact to a pinned place in your Places, that contact automatically receives your ETA whenever you start turn-by-turn navigation to that location.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Places, then tap Pinned. See Add a pin to your Places.
  3. Tap [Image: the Information button], then tap Add Person.
  4. Search for a contact, tap to add them, then tap [Image: the Done button].
  5. Tap the pinned location, then tap Go to start sharing your ETA.

Your location, route, and ETA are viewable until you arrive.

Turn off ETA sharing

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Maps.
  3. Scroll down, then turn off Share ETA.

Note: Standard carrier data and text rates may apply.

People using iOS 13.1, iPadOS 13.1, or later receive a Maps notification with your ETA, and they can track your progress in Maps. People using earlier versions receive the notification through iMessage. People using other mobile devices receive an SMS message.

When you’re near the person you’re looking for and both of you have a supported model, you can use Find My to get precise directions to each other’s location. See Use Precision Finding to meet up with a friend.

See alsoUse Maps on iPhoneShare your location in Messages on iPhoneNotify a friend when your location changes in Find My on iPhoneUse Check In on iPhone to let your friends know you’ve arrived

Use Maps

You can get travel directions using the Maps app, the Maps widget, Siri, CarPlay, or other devices. You can also get them on your Mac before you leave.

Note: Not all features are available in all countries or regions. See the iOS and iPadOS Feature Availability website.

Important: To get directions, iPhone must be connected to the internet, and Precise Location must be turned on. Cellular data rates may apply (see View or change cellular data settings).

Get directions

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Touch and hold anywhere on the map or enter a location in the search field.

  3. Tap Directions or tap your travel mode (driving , walking , transit , cycling , or rideshare .)

  4. Do one of the following:

    • If your starting point is My Location: Tap Go for the route you want to take. As you travel along your route, Maps speaks turn-by-turn directions to your destination.
    • If your starting point is another location: Tap Steps for the route you want to take.

You can add stops to your route.

Tip: If you know you’ll lose your internet connection on your route, you can send yourself a list of upcoming directions or download offline maps.

Use the Maps widget

To get directions to a likely destination and track your ETA during navigation, add the Maps widget to your Home Screen. The Maps widget shows you a preview of your commute so you know what to expect before you leave.

See Add, edit, and remove widgets.

Get directions using CarPlay, your Mac, or your Apple Watch

In addition to using your iPhone, you can also get directions from the following:

  • Your car: After you connect your iPhone to CarPlay, you can use CarPlay to get driving directions, estimate your arrival time, and more. See Get turn-by-turn directions with CarPlay.
  • Your Mac: Before a big trip or a day of cycling, you can plan your route on your Mac, then choose File > Share > Send to [your iPhone]. See Plan a route in the Maps User Guide for Mac.
  • Your Apple Watch: You can use Apple Watch to get driving, walking, transit, and cycling directions, which you can follow on the watch face and your iPhone. See Get directions on Apple Watch in the Apple Watch User Guide.

When you sign in to your Apple Account, you can hand off tasks between your iPhone and your other devices to see directions elsewhere.

Siri: You can use Siri to get directions and stay focused on the road. For example, ask Siri something like, “Find a charging station” or “Give me directions home.” See Use Siri to get directions.

See alsoShare your estimated time of arrival in Maps on iPhoneView a route overview or a list of turns in Maps on iPhoneDelete recent directions in Maps on iPhone

View a route overview or a list of turns

While following driving, cycling, transit, and walking directions, you can get an overview of your route and a list of upcoming turns.

Get an overview of your route

You can zoom out to see your entire route onscreen, from the starting point to the destination.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Get directions.
  3. Tap [Image: the Overview Mode button].

To return to turn-by-turn directions, tap [Image: the Turn-by-Turn Mode button].

View a list of upcoming directions

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Get directions.
  3. Tap anywhere on the route card except the Go button.
  4. Scroll down to see more directions.
  5. When finished, tap [Image: the Close button].

Share a route with someone

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Get directions.
  3. Tap anywhere on the route card except the Go button.
  4. Scroll to the bottom of the card, tap Share, then choose a way to share the route.

See alsoUse Maps on iPhoneShare your estimated time of arrival in Maps on iPhoneSave walks or hikes in Maps on iPhoneDownload offline maps on iPhone

View and manage Visited Places

The Visited Places feature helps you keep track of places you’ve been, so you can easily revisit or share them later. Use it to find past locations—like restaurants from a recent trip—and organize them into guides or share them with others. Visited Places are end-to-end encrypted, can’t be read by Apple, and appear on all your synced devices.

Note: Visited Places isn’t available in all countries or regions.

Turn on Visited Places

When you open the Maps app, you may be asked to turn on Visited Places. If not,

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Maps.
  3. Tap Location, then turn on Precise Location and Visited Places.
  4. Go back to the Settings app , then tap Privacy & Security.
  5. Tap Location Services, then turn on Location Services.
  6. Tap System Services, tap Significant Locations & Routes, then turn on Significant Locations & Routes.

View a visited place

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Places, tap Visited Places, then do any of the following:

    • Search: Search a place by name, category, address, or notes.
    • Filter: Search using a filter for date, category, or city.
    • Show all visits: Tap All Visits.

Manage a visited place

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Places, then tap Visited Places.

  3. Next to a place, tap More (on the right side of the place card), then do any of the following:

    • Add to your Places: Tap Add to Places.
    • Share a visited place: Tap Share.
    • Add a personal note: Tap Add a Note.
    • Correct a visited place: Tap Wrong Location.
    • Remove a visited place: Tap Remove.

Change how long Maps keeps your visited places

If you choose a duration for saving visited places when you set up the feature, you can change it at any time.

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Places, then tap Visited Places.
  3. Scroll to the bottom, tap Keep Visits, then choose a duration.

Clear your visited places history

  1. Go to the Maps app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Places, then tap Visited Places.
  3. Scroll to the bottom, then tap Clear History.

See alsoSearch for places in Maps on iPhoneGet information about places in Maps on iPhoneAdd places and notes to your Places in Maps on iPhoneShare places in Maps on iPhone

Apps: Measure

Measure a person’s height

On supported models, you can instantly measure a person’s height from the floor to the top of their head, hair, or hat. (You can even measure a person’s seated height.)

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.

  2. Position iPhone so that the person you want to measure appears on the screen from head to toe.

    After a moment, a line appears at the top of the person’s head (or hair, or hat), with the height measurement showing just below the line.

  3. To take a photo of the measurement, tap [Image: the Take Picture button].

  4. To save the photo, tap the screenshot in the lower-left corner, tap Done, then choose Save to Photos or Save to Files.

    You can easily access and share the height measurement image from Photos or Files on iPhone whenever you want.

To take the measurement again, turn iPhone away for a moment to reset the height.

See alsoView photos and videos on iPhone

Measure dimensions

You can use your iPhone camera to measure nearby objects—automatically detect the dimensions of rectangular objects or manually set the start and end points of a measurement.

For best results, use Measure on well-defined objects located 0.5 to 3 meters (2 to 10 feet) from iPhone. (Measurements are approximate.)

Note: You can use Measure on external displays without turning on Screen Mirroring in Control Center.

Start a measurement

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.
  2. Use the iPhone camera to slowly scan nearby objects.
  3. Position iPhone so that the object you want to measure appears on the screen.

Note: For your privacy, when you use Measure to take measurements, a green dot appears at the top of the screen to indicate your camera is in use.

Take an automatic rectangle measurement

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.
  2. Use the iPhone camera to slowly scan nearby objects.
  3. When iPhone detects the edges of a rectangular object, a white box frames the object; tap the white box or [Image: the Add button] to see the dimensions.
  4. To take a photo of your measurement, tap [Image: the Take Picture button].

Take a manual measurement

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.
  2. Align the dot at the center of the screen with the point where you want to start measuring, then tap [Image: the Add button].
  3. Slowly pan iPhone to the end point, then tap [Image: the Add button] to see the measured length.
  4. To take a photo of your measurement, tap [Image: the Take Picture button].
  5. Take another measurement, or tap Clear to start over.

Use edge guides

On supported models, you can easily measure the height and straight edges of furniture, countertops, and other objects using guide lines that appear automatically.

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.
  2. Position the dot at the center of the screen along the straight edge of an object until a guide line appears.
  3. Tap [Image: the Add button] where you want to begin measuring.
  4. Slowly pan along the guide line, then tap [Image: the Add button] at the endpoint to see the measured length.
  5. To take a photo of your measurement, tap [Image: the Take Picture button].

Use Ruler view

On supported models, you can see more detail in your measurements with Ruler view.

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.
  2. After measuring the distance between two points, move iPhone closer to the measurement line until it transforms into a ruler, showing incremental units of length.
  3. To take a photo of your measurement, tap [Image: the Take Picture button].

See alsoView and save measurements on iPhone

Use the level

Use your iPhone to determine whether an object near you is level (parallel to the ground), or how many degrees it varies from level (measurements are approximate).

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Level, then hold iPhone against an object, such as a picture frame.

    • Make an object level: Rotate the object and iPhone until you see green.

    • Match the slope: Tap the screen to capture the slope of the first object. Hold iPhone against another object and rotate both of them until the screen turns green.

      To reset the level, tap the screen again.

See alsoMeasure dimensions with iPhone

View and save measurements

On supported models, you can save a list of all the measurements you take in a single session, complete with screenshots, so you can easily share and access them whenever you need them.

  1. Go to the Measure app (in the Utilities folder) on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the History button] to see a list of your recent measurements.

    Swipe up from the top of the list to see more measurements.

  3. To save the measurements, tap Copy, open another app (for example, Notes), tap in a document, then tap Paste.

    Note: Height measurements aren’t included in this list. To save a person’s height measurement, see Measure a person’s height.

See alsoMeasure a person’s height with iPhone

Apps: Messages

About iMessage

iMessage is a secure messaging service that you can use to send and receive text messages in the Messages app on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

If someone sends a message to your email address or phone number using iMessage, you receive the message on all your Apple devices that are set up to receive messages sent to that email address or phone number. When you view an iMessage conversation, you see all messages sent from any device, so you can keep in touch with others wherever you are.

You need an Apple Account to use some iMessage features. If you’ve made purchases from the iTunes Store or App Store or you’ve signed in to iCloud, you have an Apple Account.

Some things to know about communicating in iMessage:

  • You can send texts over Wi-Fi or cellular service.

  • Texts you send and receive using iMessage don’t count against your SMS, MMS, or RCS allowances in your cellular messaging plan, but cellular data rates may apply.

  • When you communicate with others who also use iMessage on an Apple device, the texts appear in blue bubbles. (SMS, MMS, and RCS messages appear in green bubbles.)

    Messages are sent with iMessage when you see a blue [Image: the Send button] send button. A green send button indicates the message is sent with SMS, MMS, or RCS.

  • In a conversation, you can see if someone’s writing a message. If someone has read receipts turned on, you can also see if they’ve opened your message.

  • You can use a wider range of apps and features, like text formatting, inline replies, editing, unsending, scheduling, backgrounds, polls, Memoji, drawings, collaboration, group conversation management, and more.

  • A greater range of options are available when you react with Tapbacks, send audio messages, or send via satellite.

  • When you use iMessage, you can report spam messages to Apple and screen unknown senders.

  • For security, messages sent using iMessage are end-to-end encrypted before they’re sent, and you can also use Contact Key Verification.

See alsoTurn on iMessageSet up Messages on iPhoneSend and reply to messages on iPhoneApple Support article: What is the difference between iMessage, RCS, and SMS/MMS?

Add backgrounds

You can add a background to an iMessage conversation. Other people in the conversation see the background on their devices too and can change the background for the group.

Note: To add, view, or change conversation backgrounds, you must use iMessage on iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, watchOS 26, visionOS 26, or later.

Use a dynamic background

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation where you want to add a background.

  3. Tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation, then tap Backgrounds.

  4. Tap Color, Sky, Water, or Aurora.

  5. Swipe left to choose an option.

    Tip: For Color, tap the swatches in the bottom corners to adjust the colors.

  6. Tap [Image: the Done button] to add the background to your conversation.

[Embedded video omitted]

Use a photo as a background

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation where you want to add a photo to the background.

  3. Tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation, then tap Backgrounds.

  4. Tap Photo, then tap to select a photo from your library.

    Tip: If someone shared a photo you want to use as a background, touch and hold the photo in the message, then tap Set as Background.

  5. Do any of the following:

    • Crop the image: Pinch in or out.
    • Remove the color: Swipe left to Black & White.
    • Apply a color filter: Swipe left to Duotone or Color Wash, then tap the color swatch to change the palette.

  6. Tap [Image: the Done button] to add the background to your conversation.

You can set conversations to showcase backgrounds when you return to them. Go to Settings > Apps > Messages, then turn on Start with Photos Visible.

If Apple Intelligence* is turned on, you can use Image Playground to create one-of-a-kind images for the background of your conversations. See Use Apple Intelligence in Messages.

Note: You can have your (or a family member’s) iPhone receive warnings before a background image containing sensitive content is sent or received. See Receive warnings about sensitive content or Check for sensitive images and videos.

Revert to a plain background

Note: Removing a background affects all participants in a conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Go to the conversation with a background you want to remove.
  3. Tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation, then tap Backgrounds.
  4. Tap None.

Turn conversation backgrounds off

When you turn conversation backgrounds off, others in a conversation still see any background chosen for a conversation.

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Messages.
  3. Turn Conversation Backgrounds off.

*Apple Intelligence is available in beta with support for the following languages: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese. Some features may not be available in all languages or regions. For more information on language and feature availability and system requirements, see the Apple Support article How to get Apple Intelligence.

Collaborate on projects

In the Messages app , you can send a text message to invite people to collaborate on a project, and everyone in the conversation is added to the document, spreadsheet, or other shared file.

Note: To start collaborating on a project with Messages, you and your recipients must be using iMessage with iOS 16, iPadOS 16, macOS 13, watchOS 9, visionOS 1, or later, and you must first save the content somewhere it can be accessed by others, such as iCloud Drive. For iPhone apps, you may need to turn on iCloud to use their collaboration features. See Set up iCloud on all your devices in the iCloud User Guide.

Invite people to collaborate

You can invite people to collaborate on a project from another app, and then discuss your content in Messages. Share files from apps like Notes, Freeform, Reminders, Safari, Keynote, Numbers, Pages, and more, as long as you first turn on their collaboration features in iCloud settings and save the content somewhere it can be accessed by others, such as iCloud Drive.

The process for inviting someone to collaborate depends on the app. Here’s one way you might start a collaboration in a supported app:

  1. Select the file you want to share, then tap [Image: the Share button], or tap Collaborate.

  2. Make sure Collaborate (rather than Send Copy) is selected, then tap the group or individual you want to collaborate with. If you don’t see the group or person listed, tap [Image: the Messages app icon].

    The suggested icons may correspond with groups or individuals with active FaceTime calls or recent Messages conversations.

  3. A Messages conversation opens with the invitation ready to send. Add a note (optional), then tap [Image: the Send button].

After you invite participants in Messages, you can work on the project in the other app and return to the Messages conversation by tapping the Collaborate button in that app.

When someone edits the file, you see updates at the top of the Messages thread. To return to the shared project and see changes, tap an update.

Note: Your participants may need to accept your invitation or join the shared item before they can interact with it or see any updates.

Collaborate on a project in Messages

After you share your project, you see activity updates at the top of the Messages conversation whenever someone makes an edit.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation that contains the invitation to the project you’ve started collaborating on, then do any of the following to return to the project:

    • Tap the file in your conversation to open it.
    • If you see an update at the top of the conversation, tap Show.
    • Tap the icon of the participant or group at the top of the screen, scroll to Collaboration, then tap the shared project.

When you make any changes or edits to the project, your participants get updates in the conversation.

Note: If you add a new person to a group conversation, you have to grant them access to the projects you’re collaborating on. If they’ve been added to the group conversation recently, you can tap a notification at the top of screen to add them. Or invite them to collaborate.

Manage the collaboration and group

If you share a project with two or more people in a Messages conversation, you can add or remove participants.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation you want to manage, then tap the group icon at the top of the conversation to open details about the group’s conversation.

  3. Do any of the following:

    • Add new participants: Tap Add, then add contacts. (You may need to scroll down to see Add.)

      If you started collaborating with just one other person, you must start a new conversation to add people to the collaboration.

      Note: You must add new participants to any files that were shared in the conversation before they joined. As you add participants, a notification appears at the top of the conversation. Tap Show in the notification to review the previously shared files you can add new participants to.

    • Remove a participant from the conversation: Touch and hold their icon, then tap Remove from Group.

      Important: The apps where the collaboration happens usually control access to the project. Check participant access in the app itself to remove viewing or editing privileges completely.

The group of people in the Messages collaboration and the group collaborating on the file may not match. For example, you may invite people to collaborate on the file outside of Messages. Or you may have two different groups in Messages, each with its own collaboration conversation.

When you add someone to a document you’ve shared with others earlier, you have the option of adding them to an existing conversation or keeping the conversations separate. People added to conversations aren’t able to read messages sent before they joined the conversation.

Stop collaborating on a project in Messages

The apps where the collaboration happens usually control access to the project. For example, if you’re collaborating on a document in the Pages app, the Pages settings take precedence over the Messages settings. You can, however, unsend or delete the invitation from the conversation just as you would any other message.

Important: When you delete an invitation from a thread, that conversation is no longer associated with the collaboration, but it doesn’t remove participants from the file. Check participant access in the app to remove viewing or editing privileges completely.

Create and send Memoji

You can design your own personalized Memoji—choose skin tone, glasses, body, and more. You can create multiple Memoji to use in different contexts. Each Memoji—even the ones you create—automatically generates a range of poses and expressions. On supported models, you can send animated Memoji messages that record your voice and mirror your facial expressions.

Create Memoji

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, tap [Image: the Add button].

  3. Tap Memoji. (You may have to swipe up.)

  4. Tap [Image: the Add Memoji button].

    Tip: To make a new Memoji whose outfit or appearance differs slightly from one you already have, tap to select it, tap [Image: the Edit button], then tap Duplicate.

  5. Tap each feature (Skin, Hairstyle, and others to the right) and choose the options you want.

  6. Tap [Image: the Done button] to save the Memoji to your collection.

Send animated Memoji or Memoji recordings

On supported models, you can send Memoji messages that record your voice and mirror your facial expressions.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, tap [Image: the Add button].

  3. Tap Memoji, then swipe and tap to choose a Memoji.

  4. Tap [Image: the Record button] to record your facial expressions and voice, then tap [Image: the Recording button] to stop.

    Tap Replay to review your message.

  5. Tap [Image: the Send Recording button] to send your message or [Image: the Discard Recording button] to cancel.

You can also capture your movements, facial expressions, and voice in Memoji when you use video effects in a video call.

See alsoCreate your own emoji with Genmoji on iPhoneDraw and handwrite messages on iPhoneTake and edit photos or videos in Messages on iPhoneAdd emoji, Memoji, and stickers with the iPhone keyboard

Delete messages and attachments

You can delete text messages, attachments, and entire conversations from your iPhone anytime, without affecting what your recipients see.

Tip: Use Undo send to retract (within 2 minutes) a message you sent accidentally, deleting it from both your phone and your recipient’s phone.

Deleted messages and attachments remain in your Recently Deleted folder for up to 30 days, and you can recover them.

Delete messages and attachments

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Open a conversation, touch and hold a message bubble or attachment, then tap More.
  3. Select the messages or attachments you want to delete, then tap [Image: the Delete button].

You can also delete a conversation entirely.

Delete multiple photos, videos, or other attachments

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation.

  3. Tap a category, such as Photos.

    Tip: To see only only one kind of image, tap [Image: the Filter button] at the bottom left, then tap Screenshots, Videos, or Photos.

  4. Tap Edit, then tap Select.

  5. Tap each attachment you want to delete, tap [Image: the Delete button], then tap to confirm the number of attachments you want to delete.

Delete a conversation

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, do one of the following:

    • Swipe left on the conversation, then tap [Image: the Delete button].
    • Touch and hold the conversation, then tap Delete.

Delete multiple conversations

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. At the top of the conversation list, tap Edit.
  3. Tap Select Messages, then select conversations you want to delete.
  4. Tap [Image: the Delete button], then tap Delete.

Permanently remove recently deleted messages and attachments

Deleted messages and attachments remain in the Recently Deleted folder for 30 days, but you can permanently remove them before that.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the Filter button] at the top of the conversation list, then tap Recently Deleted.

  3. Select the conversations whose messages you want to delete permanently, tap [Image: the Delete button], then tap Delete.

    Important: This can’t be undone.

Automatically delete old messages

You can delete messages and attachments that are older than 30 days or a year old, on an ongoing basis.

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Messages.
  3. Scroll down, tap Keep Messages (below Message History), then choose an option.

Important: If you choose an option other than Forever, your conversations (including all attachments) are automatically removed after the specified time period elapses.

If you use Messages in iCloud, deleting a message or conversation on your iPhone deletes it from all your devices where Messages in iCloud is turned on. See Keep your messages up to date with iCloud in the iCloud User Guide.

Note: Deleting messages only affects your iPhone and other Apple devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. You can’t delete messages, attachments, and conversations for anyone else.

To delete everything (not just your messages), see Erase iPhone.

See alsoUnsend and edit messages on iPhoneScreen and filter text messages on iPhoneAutomatically delete one-time verification codes

Draw and handwrite messages

You can send messages with handwriting, doodling, and more.

You need iMessage to exchange drawn or handwritten messages.

Send a Digital Touch gesture, animation, or effect

With Digital Touch, you can send animated sketches, taps, kisses, heartbeats, and more, on their own or as an effect on a photo or video.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, tap [Image: the Add button].

  3. Swipe up, tap Digital Touch, then do one of the following:

    • Send an animated gesture: Tap or touch and hold with one or two fingers. Your gesture is sent automatically when you finish it.

      Touch and hold the color dot to choose a color for the one-finger taps.

      Note: If you have Apple Watch or another sensor that records heartbeat data, Messages may use the recorded data when you touch and hold with two fingers to send a heartbeat.

    • Send an animated drawing: Draw with one finger.

      You can change the color, then start drawing again.

    • Add an effect to a new image: Tap [Image: the Camera button], then tap [Image: the Take Picture button] to take a photo or [Image: the Record Video button] to record a video.

      To take a new photo or video, or to erase anything you draw on your preview, tap [Image: the Back to Preview button].

  4. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send your drawing or image, or tap [Image: the Close button] to delete it.

To send an animated doodle on a white background, see Send a handwritten message or doodle.

Send a handwritten message or doodle

Use your finger to write a message or draw a doodle. Recipients see what you wrote or drew, re-created before their eyes.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. In a conversation, rotate iPhone to landscape orientation.
  3. Tap [Image: the Handwriting key] on the keyboard.
  4. Write a message with your finger or choose a saved message at the bottom, then tap Done.
  5. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send your message or [Image: the Remove app from message button] to cancel.

After you create and send a handwritten message, the message is saved at the bottom of the handwriting screen. To use the saved message again, tap it. To delete the saved message, touch and hold it until the messages jiggle, then tap [Image: the Delete button].

To send a doodle on a black background, see Send a Digital Touch gesture, animation, or effect.

See alsoSend and reply to messages on iPhoneSend stickers in Messages on iPhoneTake and edit photos or videos in Messages on iPhoneUse iMessage apps in Messages on iPhone

Format text and animate messages

You can express yourself in the messages you send by formatting or animating the text in your message, the message bubble, or the entire screen.

Note: To send and receive messages with text formatting or text effects, you and your recipients must be using iMessage. Messages appear in plain text when sent to devices using older or other operating systems.

Format or animate text within messages

Format the text in your messages with bold, italics, and underlining, or add playful, animated effects like explode or shake to any letter, word, or sentence—even emoji—in texts you send using iMessage.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, enter a message, then select the text you want to format or animate.

    The Messages app may suggest effects to apply as you enter your message.

  3. Tap [Image: the Text Format button] above the keyboard, then select your preferred formats (bold, italic, underline, or strikethrough) or animated effect (big, small, shake, nod, explode, ripple, bloom, or jitter).

  4. Tap [Image: the Send button].

You can format or apply effects to a single word, emoji, single word, emoji, sentence, or your entire message. Tap [Image: the Text Format button] before entering the text you want to format or apply effects to.

Animate the message bubble

Use effects to animate the message bubble: you can send a message with Slam or Loud so that it appears to pop out, or use Gentle so it arrives softly. You can even send a personal message with Invisible Ink that remains blurred until the recipient swipes to reveal it.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. In a conversation, enter a message or insert an image or link.
  3. Touch and hold [Image: the Send button], then tap a gray dot to preview a bubble effect.
  4. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send the message with the effect or [Image: the Close button] to cancel the effect and return to your message.

If you don’t see a bubble effect or want to turn off effects on messages you receive, see Customize onscreen motion.

Animate effects over the full screen

You can send messages with full-screen effects—such as lively lasers, a moving spotlight, or echoing bubbles—that play when your recipient gets your message.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. In a conversation, enter a message or insert a photo or Memoji.
  3. Touch and hold [Image: the Send button], then tap Screen.
  4. Swipe left to preview different screen effects.
  5. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send the message or [Image: the Close button] to cancel the effect and return to your message.

Messages automatically uses the following screen effects for specific text strings:

  • Balloons for “Happy birthday”
  • Confetti for “Congratulations”
  • Fireworks for “Happy New Year”

If you don’t see a full-screen effect or want to turn off effects on messages you receive, see Customize onscreen motion.

See alsoSend stickers in Messages on iPhoneDraw and handwrite messages on iPhoneUse iMessage apps in Messages on iPhone

Forward and share messages

You can forward one or more text messages in a conversation to a different recipient.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Touch and hold a message bubble you want to forward, then tap More.
  3. Tap to select one or more messages to forward, then tap Image: the Forward button.
  4. Enter recipients, then tap [Image: the Send button].

Tip: To show the message bubbles and timestamps just as they appear in a conversation, send a screenshot as an attached image instead of forwarding messages.

To see the same messages on other devices you use, see Sync messages on all your Apple devices.

Get started with Messages

In the Messages app , you can exchange texts, photos, videos, and more, with individuals, businesses, and groups. You can express yourself with backgrounds and animations, share TV shows and music, and use Messages to collaborate with others.

Set up iMessage and sync across devices

When you and a friend both sign in to iMessage, you can send each other unlimited messages, no matter where you are in the world. Go to Settings > Apps > Messages, then turn on iMessage. To see the same messages you get on your iPhone on your other Apple devices, tap Text Message Forwarding, then turn on your other devices in the list. Be sure to sign in to the same Apple Account on the other devices, too.

Chat as a group

You can chat with several people at once—like your family or a work group. Tap [Image: the Compose button], enter the names of the people in the group, then type your message, or tap [Image: the Dictate button] to dictate it. To name the group, tap the group icons at the top of the conversation, tap Edit, then tap Edit Name and Photo.

Go beyond texting

You don’t have to limit your communication to text. To add emoji, tap [Image: the Emoji key] or [Image: the Next Keyboard key] on your keyboard. To add media, polls, location sharing, and more, tap [Image: the Add button] next to the text field.

Schedule a message to deliver later

If it’s too late at night or too important to forget, schedule your message for a future time, instead of sending it as soon as you finish it. Tap [Image: the Add button], tap Send Later, choose a time, then tap [Image: the Send button].

Group conversations

You can send a group text message, name it, and assign it an icon to find it more easily. In a group conversation, you can call people’s attention to specific messages and even collaborate on projects.

Start a group conversation

You can send a message to multiple people to start a group conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, tap [Image: the Compose button] at the bottom right of the screen.

  3. Tap the To field, then enter the phone number, contact name, or Apple Account of each recipient.

    To choose group members from your contacts, tap [Image: the Add Contact button] in the To field.

    Note: If one or more of your recipients isn’t using iMessage, messages appear in green bubbles instead of blue ones.

  4. Tap the text field, enter a message or tap [Image: the Add button] (to the left of the text field) to send a photo, video, poll, or another item with iMessage apps.

  5. Tap [Image: the Send button].

Add someone to an existing group conversation

If you have at least two other people in a group conversation, you can add additional contacts.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap the group conversation you want to add someone to.

  3. Tap the group icon at the top of the conversation, then tap Add.

  4. Enter the phone number, contact name, or Apple Account of each recipient.

    To add group members from your contacts, tap [Image: the Add Contact button] in the To field.

  5. Tap [Image: the Done button] to save your changes.

Note: If the group includes someone who hasn’t turned on iMessage, follow the onscreen instructions to start a new group.

If you only have one other person in the conversation, you need to start a new group conversation to add someone else.

To remove someone from a group conversation in iMessage, touch and hold their icon, then tap Remove from Group.

In iOS 26 or later, you can add new contacts introduced in group conversations. See Create a contact.

Leave a group conversation

You can leave a group chat if there are at least three other participants in the conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap the group conversation you want to leave.

  3. Tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation.

  4. Scroll down and tap Leave This Conversation or Delete and Block This Conversation. (Learn more about deleting and blocking conversations.)

    Blocked conversations are moved to the Recently Deleted folder, where you can recover them.

If you want to stay in a group chat but stop receiving its notifications, mute the conversation instead.

Mention people in a group conversation

You can mention someone by name in a group conversation to call their attention to a specific message, and they’ll get a notification. Depending on their settings, the person you mention may be notified even if they have the conversation muted.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, begin typing a contact’s name in the text field.

  3. Tap the contact’s name when it appears.

    You can also mention a contact in Messages by typing @ followed by the contact’s name.

    To change whether you get notifications when your name is mentioned in Messages, go to Settings  > Apps > Messages, then turn on or off Notify Me.

Name a group conversation

You can name a group chat and choose an icon* to represent the conversation. Everyone who has turned on iMessage sees the new name and icon.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap the group icon at the top of the conversation.
  3. Tap Edit, tap Edit Name & Photo, then choose an option.

Send or request money

In group iMessage conversations in iOS 26 or later, you can send money to someone in a group chat or make a request of the group to split bills, organize gifts, or pay someone back, then track payments in the Wallet app. See Send, request, and receive payments with Apple Cash in Messages.

*Availability varies by region.

See alsoCollaborate on projects with Messages on iPhoneShare content in Messages on iPhoneApple Support article: Send a group text message

Keep track of messages

You can catch up on text messages you missed, mark messages as unread, and pin and unpin conversations to prioritize messages in the conversation list.

Catch up on messages you missed

If you receive messages while you have notifications paused or you’re away from your iPhone, you can jump to the first message you haven’t seen in a conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open an unread conversation, then tap [Image: the Catch up button].

    Your view of the conversation moves up to the first unread message.

Mark messages as unread

When you don’t have time to respond, you can mark conversations as unread so you can return to them later.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, do one of the following:

    • Swipe right on a conversation to mark it as unread.
    • Drag right and tap [Image: the Mark as Unread button].

Tip: You can also mark several messages as unread at the same time. In the conversation list, tap Edit, tap Select Messages, select the conversations you want to mark as unread, then tap Unread in the bottom-left corner.

See a list of your unread messages

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, tap [Image: the Filter button], then tap Unread.

    A checkmark appears next to Unread, and the icon turns blue [Image: the Filter button] to indicate that filtering is on.

  3. To see both your read and unread messages again, tap [Image: the Filter button], then tap to deselect Unread.

Tip: To mark all your unread messages as read, tap Edit, tap Select Messages, then tap Read All.

Pin a conversation

You can pin specific conversations to the top of the conversation list so the people you contact most always come first in the list. Pinned conversations appear as larger icons at the top of your conversation list.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Touch and hold a conversation, then tap Pin.

Unpin a conversation

You can unpin pinned conversations so that they no longer appear at the top of the conversation list.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Touch and hold a pinned conversation, then do one of the following:

    • Drag the message to the bottom of the list, and let go.
    • Tap Unpin.

Pin shared items

You can pin certain shared items—such as links or collaboration invitations—within a conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Touch and hold a message, then tap Pin.
  3. To find pinned items, tap the contact or group icon at the top of the conversation, then tap a category (such as Links). Pinned items appear at the top.

To unpin a pinned item, touch and hold it in the message, then tap Unpin. If you’re in the Links or Documents tab, touch and hold the item, tap Show in Conversation, touch and hold it in the message, then tap Unpin.

See message summaries

Apple Intelligence* can show you a summary of unread messages in a conversation. See Use Apple Intelligence in Messages.

*Apple Intelligence is available in beta with support for the following languages: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese. Some features may not be available in all languages or regions. For more information on language and feature availability and system requirements, see the Apple Support article How to get Apple Intelligence.

Poll people in a conversation

You can send a poll in any iMessage conversation to decide what to eat, which movie to see, where to travel, when to meet, and more. Everyone in the conversation can contribute options and watch as votes come in.

Note: You must use iMessage on iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, watchOS 26, visionOS 26, or later to start, see, or vote in a poll. Those who can’t see it receive a message that a poll was sent to the group.

[Embedded video omitted]

Start a poll

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. In a conversation, tap [Image: the Add button], then tap Polls.
  3. Tap each row to add options. A poll can have up to 12 options.
  4. Tap [Image: the Send button].

Tip: Turn on Apple Intelligence* to get suggestions for polls.

Vote in a poll

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Open a conversation with a poll in it.
  3. Tap an option to add your vote. Tap again to remove your vote. You can vote for none or all of the options.

Add an option to a poll

Anyone participating in a poll can add an option to it.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open a conversation with a poll in it.

  3. Tap Add Choice, then enter another option.

  4. Tap [Image: the Send button] to add the option to the poll.

    Note: Options are added without votes. Tap to vote for any option you add.

Check on the results of a poll

You can see how people voted or who hasn’t voted yet.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Open a conversation with a poll in it.
  3. Touch and hold the poll, then tap Poll Details.

*Apple Intelligence is available in beta with support for the following languages: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese. Some features may not be available in all languages or regions. For more information on language and feature availability and system requirements, see the Apple Support article How to get Apple Intelligence.

React with Tapbacks

Tapbacks give you a quick and easy way to respond to a message, such as a heart, a thumbs-up or thumbs-down, laughter, exclamation points, a question mark, and any sticker, Memoji, or emoji.

React with a Tapback

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open a conversation.

  3. Double-tap (or touch and hold) a message.

  4. Swipe left to see suggested emoji and stickers, or tap [Image: the Emoji button], then tap to choose any of the following kinds of Tapbacks:

    • Other emoji: Tap [Image: the Emoji button] (jump to other emoji categories with icons to the right of [Image: the Emoji button]).
    • Stickers: Tap [Image: the Live Stickers button].

The Tapback is attached to a specific message in a conversation, and everyone who’s part of the conversation can see it.

Find out who sent a Tapback

If there’s more than one Tapback for a message, they appear in a stack. You can find out who added each Tapback.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open a conversation with Tapbacks.

  3. Tap a stack of Tapbacks.

    Senders and their tapbacks appear near the top of the screen.

Edit or remove your Tapback

You can only edit or remove Tapbacks you added. You can’t edit or remove Tapbacks other people added.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open a conversation.

  3. Tap your Tapback, then do one of the following:

    • Use a different Tapback: Tap a different emoji, Memoji, or sticker.
    • Remove the Tapback: Tap the same Tapback you used (so it’s not highlighted).

You can only add one Tapback per message. If you want to send additional stickers, see Place stickers on a conversation.

See alsoFormat text and animate messages on iPhoneSend stickers in Messages on iPhoneSend and save GIFs in Messages on iPhoneAdd emoji, Memoji, and stickers with the iPhone keyboard

Recover deleted messages

You can recover deleted text messages you deleted on your iPhone.

You can restore messages you deleted for up to 30 days.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap [Image: the Filter button] at the top of the conversation list, then tap Recently Deleted.
  3. Select the conversations whose messages you want to restore, then tap Recover.
  4. Tap Recover Messages.

If you use Messages in iCloud, recovering a message or conversation on your iPhone recovers it on all your devices where Messages in iCloud is turned on. See Keep your messages up to date with iCloud in the iCloud User Guide.

Note: Deleting and recovering messages only affects your iPhone and other Apple devices where you’re signed in to the same Apple Account. You can’t recover messages, attachments, and conversations for anyone else.

Once you recover a blocked conversation whose participants haven’t all turned on iMessage, incoming messages are no longer automatically deleted.

Any message that you remove from a conversation using Undo Send is permanently deleted. Audio messages that expire before being saved aren’t recoverable. See Send and receive audio messages.

See alsoDelete messages and attachments in Messages on iPhoneScreen and filter text messages on iPhoneAutomatically delete one-time verification codesApple Support article: Recover deleted text messages on your iPhone or iPad

Report spam and block senders

You can report spam messages to Apple, recover messages from the Spam folder that were incorrectly marked as spam, and block specific contacts to stop receiving their messages.

Report spam messages

When you use iMessage, you can report spam messages to Apple. Depending on your carrier and country or region, reporting spam you receive with SMS, MMS, or RCS shares this information with your carrier and its affiliates.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Do one of the following:

    • If you haven’t opened the message: Swipe left on the message, tap [Image: the Delete button], then tap Delete and Report Spam.

    • If you’ve already opened the message: A Report Spam link appears at the bottom of any message from any unknown sender. Tap Report Spam, then tap Delete and Report Spam.

      Note: You can’t report a message after you’ve replied to it.

    • If you don’t see the option to report spam messages you receive with SMS, MMS, or RCS: Contact your carrier. See the Apple Support article Wireless carrier support and features for iPhone.

If you received the message with iMessage, it’s sent to Apple with the sender’s information, and the message is permanently deleted from your iPhone.

If you accidentally report and delete messages, you can recover them.

Reporting spam doesn’t prevent the sender from sending messages. To avoid receiving their messages, block the contact.

To avoid getting incoming messages from new numbers, you can filter them. See Screen and filter messages from unknown senders, above.

Recover messages in the Spam folder

When spam is detected, it’s moved to the spam folder and doesn’t appear in your conversation list. You can check to see if messages are inadvertently marked as spam.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the Filter button] at the top right of the conversation list, then tap Spam.

  3. Tap a message that isn’t spam, tap Not Spam, then tap Move to Messages.

    The conversation moves to your main conversation list, where you can send a reply. Tap [Image: the Filter button], then tap Messages.

Spam filtering is on by default. To turn it on or off, tap [Image: the Filter button], tap Manage Filtering, then turn on or off “Filter spam.”

Block messages from a specific person or phone number

When you block a specific contact or phone number, messages from that person or number aren’t delivered. The person sending the message doesn’t know that their messages are blocked.

Note: When you block a contact in Messages, that contact is also blocked in Mail, Phone, FaceTime, Calendar, and other apps. See Prevent contacts from communicating with you.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation with the person you want to block, then tap the person’s icon at the top.

  3. Tap Info, scroll down, then tap Block Contact.

    You can remove someone’s access to shared items. See Manage information sharing with Safety Check.

Tip: You can’t block a group conversation, so instead of blocking all the people in the group, you can simply leave it or stop its notifications.

If you’re still having trouble with unwanted messages, see the Apple Support article Block phone numbers, contacts, and emails on your iPhone or iPad.

Check who you blocked

If you’re not getting someone’s messages, you can check if they’re in your Blocked Contacts.

When you block a contact in Messages, that contact is also blocked in Mail, Phone, FaceTime, Calendar, and other apps.

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Privacy & Security, tap Blocked Contacts, then do any of the following:

    • Unblock a number you’ve blocked: Tap [number] Unknown, swipe left on a number in the list, then tap Unblock. Or tap Edit, then tap [Image: the Remove button].
    • Add additional contacts or numbers directly to the list: Tap Add Blocked Contact.

A sender can’t find out if they’re blocked.

Tip: Another way to prevent unwanted messages is to allow your contacts only when you block messages with Screen Time.

To change how the notifications appear and more, you can set your notification options.

To pause notifications from Messages, turn on Do Not Disturb or another Focus.

To screen and filter messages from unknown senders, see Screen and filter texts.

To learn about other ways you can report and prevent unwanted messages, see the Apple Support article Recognize and avoid phishing messages, phony support calls, and other scams.

See alsoKeep track of messages on iPhoneStop, mute, and change message notifications on iPhoneDelete messages and attachments in Messages on iPhoneManage information sharing with Safety Check on iPhone

Schedule a text message to send later

If it’s too late at night or too important to forget, you can schedule a text message to be sent at a later time.

Note: You must be using iMessage. Your recipient can use any device, and they won’t know that the message was scheduled. You need to be online to reschedule, edit, or delete a scheduled message.

Schedule a message

You can schedule a message up to 14 days into the future.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation where you want to schedule a message or start a conversation.

  3. Tap [Image: the Add button], then tap Send Later.

  4. Tap the time to open the scheduler, then choose when you want to send your message.

    The border of the text field turns into a dashed line, and the time your message will be sent appears at the top of the message.

  5. Enter a message, then tap [Image: the Send button].

The message appears with a dashed line until it’s time to send it, and it’s delivered even if all your devices are offline.

Note: Scheduled messages are encrypted and stored on Apple servers only until they’re sent. When a message is sent, it’s removed from Apple servers, the balloon becomes a solid color, and its dashed line disappears.

Change the time to send a message

You can reschedule a message until its delivery time.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation with the message you want to reschedule.

    If you don’t see your message, scroll down to the bottom of the conversation. Scheduled messages may appear below sent messages.

  3. Tap Edit beside the date (above your scheduled message), then do any of the following:

    • Reschedule it: Tap Edit Time, choose a new time, then tap away from the schedule to commit the new time.
    • Send it immediately: Tap Send Message.

Edit a scheduled message

You can edit a scheduled message until its delivery time.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation with the scheduled message you want to edit.

    If you don’t see your message, scroll down to the bottom of the conversation. Scheduled messages may appear below sent messages.

  3. Touch and hold the message bubble, then tap Edit.

  4. Make any changes, then tap [Image: the Send Edit button] to resend with edits or [Image: the Cancel Edit button] to revert.

Delete a scheduled message

When you delete a message before its scheduled time, it’s canceled and not delivered to the recipient.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Go to the conversation with the scheduled message you want to delete.

    If you don’t see your message, scroll down to the bottom of the conversation. Scheduled messages may appear below sent messages.

  3. Touch and hold the message you want to cancel, then tap Delete.

See alsoUnsend and edit messages on iPhoneTurn read receipts on or off in Messages on iPhoneDelete messages and attachments in Messages on iPhone

Screen and filter texts

You can reduce the number of unwanted text messages you receive when you screen and filter messages from unknown senders and turn off business alerts.

Screen and filter messages from unknown senders

You can prevent unknown senders from texting you directly. Their messages are filtered other folders, and you don’t get notified about them unless you want to be.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the Filter button] at the top right of the conversation list, then tap Manage Filtering.

  3. Turn on Screen Unknown Senders.

  4. If you want to allow notifications from some unknown senders, tap Allow Notifications, then turn on or off those categories. (Options vary by country and region.)

    For example, you can allow notifications for time-sensitive texts, like verification codes.

  5. To detect and filter SMS, MMS, and RCS messages from unknown senders into folders for Transactions and Promotions, tap [Image: the Back button], tap Text Message Filter, then turn on Text Message Filter and third-party message filtering extensions you install.

    Note: Filters apply to promotions and transactions (or whatever your third-party message filtering extension offers). Text message filtering doesn’t apply to any sender you’ve replied to three times or more. Try blocking or reporting those senders.

Review messages from unknown senders and mark them as known

A known sender can be someone you’ve marked as known or added to the Contacts app. If you want messages from someone in Unknown Senders to appear in your conversation list, or if you can’t open a link sent by an unknown sender, make them a known sender.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap [Image: the Filter button] at the top right of the conversation list, then tap Unknown Senders.

  3. Do any of the following:

    • Tap the message from the sender whose messages you want to see in your conversation list, then tap Mark as Known.
    • Tap the sender’s email address or phone number at the top of the conversation, then tap Create New Contact.

Until you mark a sender as known or add them as a contact, any future messages are filtered to Unknown Senders.

Turn off business alerts

Some businesses send alerts and updates on your orders and other transactions. You can turn these off.

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Apps, then tap Messages.

  3. Turn off any of the following:

    • RCS Business Messages: Tap RCS Messaging, then turn RCS Business Messages off. (Availability varies by carrier and country.)
    • Apple Messages for Business: Tap Messages for Business, then turn Business Updates off.

You can also report spam messages when you receive them.

See Apple Messages for Business & Privacy.

Tip: Another way to prevent unwanted messages is to allow messages only from your contacts with Screen Time.

To change how the notifications appear and more, you can set your notification options.

To pause notifications from Messages, turn on Do Not Disturb or another Focus.

To learn about other ways you can report and prevent unwanted messages, see the Apple Support article Recognize and avoid phishing messages, phony support calls, and other scams.

See alsoKeep track of messages on iPhoneStop, mute, and change message notifications on iPhoneDelete messages and attachments in Messages on iPhoneManage information sharing with Safety Check on iPhone

Search

You can search for text messages and attachments, using different criteria to narrow your results.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Tap the search field below the conversation list.

  3. Enter what you’re looking for (such as a word or phrase).

  4. To filter your search, do any of the following:

    • Limit your search to one person or conversation: Start by typing a person’s name, tap “Messages with” or “Messages in,” then tap other criteria that appear or add any text you want to find in your conversation.
    • Limit your search to types of shared items: Begin your search with a search term—such as Photo, Link, Wallet (for passes). When a filter appears near the top of the screen, tap it to add it to filter the search.
    • Combine search criteria: Add another search term or filter.

  5. Tap [Image: the Search button], then tap a message in the results list to read it.

The search field also opens suggestions—such as conversations, photos, locations, links, and more. Tap any suggestion to quickly jump to a conversation.

See alsoSearch with Spotlight on iPhoneSearch for photos and videos on iPhoneShare content in Messages on iPhoneKeep track of messages on iPhone

Send and receive audio messages

You can record and send audio messages, along with transcripts of what’s said in the message. Audio messages are automatically deleted to save space on your iPhone, but if you want to save them, you can.

Note: Audio message transcription is available in select languages. See the iOS and iPadOS Feature Availability website.

Record and send an audio message

Instead of writing a text message, you can record an audio message that can be played right in the Messages conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In a conversation, tap [Image: the Add button].

  3. Tap Audio, then begin speaking.

  4. Tap [Image: the Stop button] to pause or end your recording, then do any of the following to your message:

    • Send it: Tap [Image: the Send button].
    • Listen to review it: Tap [Image: the Play button].
    • Add to the end of it: Tap [Image: the Continue Recording button] (with the message duration).
    • Cancel it: Tap [Image: the Close button].

  5. Tap Keep to save an incoming or outgoing audio message on your iPhone.

    Otherwise, the recording is deleted from the conversation—on your iPhone only—2 minutes after you send or listen to it. Recipients can play your recording any time after they receive it. To save it, they need to tap Keep within 2 minutes after listening to it.

Tip: Send follow-up audio messages more quickly by touching and holding [Image: the Record Audio button] in the text field.

Audio messages are automatically transcribed in the language chosen in the sender’s Settings. To switch to another language for your outgoing messages, see Change the language and region.

Always keep audio messages

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Messages.
  3. Tap Expire (below Audio Messages), then tap Never.

Listen or reply to a recorded audio message

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. Open a conversation with an audio message, then tap [Image: the Play button] to play it.

  3. Do any of the following:

    • Slide right and left on the audio message to fast-forward or rewind.
    • Touch and hold [Image: the Play button] or [Image: the Pause button] to adjust the playback speed.

  4. Tap Keep to save an audio message in the conversation.

    To save the message in the Voice Memos app , touch and hold the audio message, then tap Save to Voice Memos.

Use Raise to Listen

When you receive an audio message, you can move your iPhone to play and reply to the message. Do either of the following:

  • Play an audio message: Raise your iPhone to your ear.
  • Reply to an audio message: Lower your iPhone and raise it to your ear again, then speak after you hear a tone. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send your reply.

Turn off Raise to Listen

If you don’t want audio messages to play when you raise your iPhone to your ear, you can turn the feature off.

  1. Go to the Settings app  on your iPhone.
  2. Tap Apps, then tap Messages.
  3. Turn off Raise to Listen.

Switch to FaceTime from Messages

You can quickly make an audio or video call instead of sending a message by switching to FaceTime. In a Messages conversation, tap [Image: the FaceTime button].

See alsoMake a recording in Voice Memos on iPhoneChange your voicemail greeting and settings on iPhoneMake FaceTime calls on iPhoneDictate text on iPhone

Send and reply to messages

You can send text messages, images, and much more. You can reply within a conversation or to specific comments in a thread. You can even use Siri to listen and respond to your messages.

To fully use all the features in the Messages app, make sure you set up Messages.

Siri: Ask Siri something like, “Read my last message from Antonio.” Learn how to use Siri.

Start a conversation

You can send a text message to one or more people to start a new conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, tap [Image: the Compose button] at the bottom right of the screen.

  3. Tap the To field, then enter the phone number, contact name, or Apple Account of each recipient.

    To choose recipients from your contacts, tap [Image: the Add Contact button] in the To field.

  4. Do any of the following:

    • Tap the text field above the keyboard, then type your message.
    • Tap [Image: the Emoji key] or [Image: the Next Keyboard key] to add emoji.
    • Tap [Image: the Dictate key] to dictate text in the language of your keyboard.
    • Tap [Image: the Add button] (to the left of the text field) to send photos, videos, stickers, polls, audio messages, your location, and more with iMessage apps.

  5. Tap [Image: the Send button] to send.

    If a message can’t be sent, an alert appears. Tap [Image: the Send Failure button] to try sending the message again.

To return to the conversation list from a conversation, tap [Image: the Back button].

If Apple Intelligence* is turned on, you can create custom emoji—called Genmoji. See Create your own emoji with Genmoji.

If you’re having problems, see the Apple Support article If you can’t send or receive messages on your iPhone or iPad.

Reply to a message

Messages are grouped by conversation in the conversation list. A dot indicates you haven’t yet read one or more messages in that conversation.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.
  2. Go to the conversation that you want to participate in.
  3. Tap the text field, create your message, then tap [Image: the Send button] to send your message.

If Apple Intelligence is turned on, you can use it to suggest a reply to a message you receive. See Use Apple Intelligence in Messages.

Tip: Find out when a message was sent to you. Drag the message bubble to the left to see timestamps for all messages in the conversation.

Reply inline to a specific message

You can respond to a specific message inline. An inline reply quotes the message you’re responding to. This keeps a busy conversation organized by clarifying which response relates to which message.

  1. Go to the Messages app on your iPhone.

  2. In the conversation list, tap the conversation that you want to participate in.

  3. Do one of the following:

    • Swipe right on the message bubble that you want to reply to.
    • Touch and hold the message bubble that you want to reply to, then tap Reply.

  4. Enter your message, then tap [Image: the Send button].

    Note: Everyone in a group conversation can see your inline reply. To reply privately, tap the group icon at the top of the conversation, touch and hold the icon of the person you want to message privately, then tap Message.

  5. To return to the main conversation, tap the blurred background.

Touch and hold a message to react with a Tapback, such as a thumbs-up or a heart.

Tip: To copy part of a message, touch and hold the message, tap Select, select the text you want to copy, then tap Copy.

Reply to messages from your Lock Screen

You can reply to messages on your Lock Screen without opening Messages. See Turn on Lock Screen features.

Send a text message from your other number

If your iPhone is set up with Dual SIM, you can tap your number to switch to your other outgoing line as you compose your message.

Why are some bubbles blue and others green?

If a message can be sent using iMessage, you see a blue Send arrow , and the message appears in a blue bubble.

If you can’t use iMessage (which happens, for example, when a recipient isn’t using an Apple device), you can use SMS, MMS, or RCS. Messages sent with SMS, MMS, or RCS appear in green bubbles.

For more information, see the Apple Support article What is the difference between iMessage, RCS, and SMS/MMS?

Note: Content may not appear as expected when you send messages to recipients who are using non-Apple devices.

Use Live Translation
